findings.reason: the author must either state that the correction drives off the ledger row itself, or record that this cited row cannot be corrected, or a node will ship a verb that cannot repair the evidence it exists for.
findings.text: the deliverable resolves the run's repository and head only through the live pointer or a rebuilt run directory (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:4826-4847 → reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:200-216), and the row this section names as evidence, reckon's r-20261121T201951227166-anchored-module-s18, has no live pointer (only r-20261121T201951227166-anchored-module-s18.json.before-pointer-repair and .json.before-wait-clear remain) and no directory under ~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/, so the verb refuses with "no run directory survives to rebuild it from" before it can reach the correction — the section's own motivating row stays wrong.

findings.reason: the deliverable and its gate are unchanged by the sentence; only the paragraph's stated consequence is imprecise.
findings.text: the closing clause "its review never matches it" is not supported: a run review is keyed on the run id and reads landed from the presence of that run's ledger row (reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:290-296 via reckon/crew/obligations.py:4666), so a wrong commit in the row does not stop the review matching the run; the harm the row does carry is that anything deriving the run's reviewed head from the row reads the wrong revision (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:1029-1034).
